relevance_note: The paper describes identifiable people with germline TNFAIP3 variants and HA20: it reports a novel missense variation "identified in three patients from the same family" and gives each of them individual-level clinical detail.
method_note: Manual extraction; no script was run, every cell was transcribed by hand and re-read against the printed Markdown. Table 1 has patients as columns; its column headers are the paper's own labels (I.1, II.1, II.2), which the text also uses, so those labels are kept. Spans for the column-based rows of Table 1 quote the row from its row label through the relevant patient's cell. Scope decision: rows were given to the three patients of the family and to the healthy mother I.2, a relative tested for the variant and reported negative for it. Table 2 is a literature table of previously reported index cases; those people are in scope, but the checklist requires one row per person per feature and, without being able to run a script, that was not workable here, so no rows were created for the 12 previously reported index cases of Table 2 nor for the relatives named in its 'Family segregation' row (father, brother, mother, sister, three other family members); the 'sisters' of the c.1639G>A column have no number, so no row was created for them either. Contradictions found: (1) the text says the c.707T>C, p.(Leu236Pro) variation 'is of uncertain significance' under ACMG criteria, whereas Table 2 gives its pathogenic significance as 'Likely pathogenic'; the variant rows record the Table 2 wording and the ACMG-criteria field is 'not reported' because no criteria codes are printed; (2) Table 2 attributes the c.305A>G, p.(Asn102Ser) column to 'Chen et al., 2020b', but reference 4 (the patient report) is Chen et al., 2020a, 2020b being the PremPS tool paper; (3) the Functional consequence cell of the c.1939A>C, p.(Thr647Pro) column cites '(Kadowaki et al., 2021)'. Inheritance: the father I.1 carries the same variation, so the daughters' variant is recorded as inherited paternal; for I.1 no parental information is given, so inheritance is 'not reported'. Table 1 uses the word 'No' in a cell; it is read as an explicit negative. 'Genital ulcers were very rare' is read as present, not excluded. A feature reported as normal or negative is recorded as the abnormality it rules out. Growth failure, cytopenia, lymphoproliferation, autoantibodies, thyroiditis, diabetes, CNS involvement, recurrent infections, lung disease and vasculitis are not addressed by the paper for anyone.
